items.difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the author proposition at source lines 707-712: the relations Term and ClTerm, which hold of the Godel number of a term or a closed term, are primitive recursive. The author proof (714-766) must encode formation sequences for terms, show that the three formation rules translate into primitive-recursive conditions on the code y of a candidate sequence using bounded quantification, derive a primitive-recursive bound on the code from the fact that every subterm starts at a distinct place inside s and has Godel number at most x, and finally obtain ClTerm by dropping the variable clause. The bound argument and the three-clause decomposition are real coding work, and the only deferred item is the auxiliary flatten routine whose primitivity the author flags inline and makes a follow-up problem.
